description:
**Severity: critical · Dimension: tail-masking** (report finding #1)

`BitVec::from_words` (`crates/gf2-core/src/bitvec.rs:204`) is the only public constructor that accepts caller-supplied words without calling `mask_tail()`. Every other constructor that could produce dirty padding masks. When a caller passes a final word with bits set above `len_bits % 64`, the padding-bits-must-be-zero invariant is broken, silently corrupting popcount, rank/select, equality, and all downstream bitwise operations.

This is the most critical correctness invariant in the crate (AGENTS.md design invariant #1).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `BitVec::from_words` calls `mask_tail()` before returning, enforcing the invariant internally.
- [hard] REQ-02: The "caller must ensure padding is zero" note is removed from the doc comment (invariant now enforced, not delegated).
- [hard] REQ-03: A regression test constructs a `BitVec` via `from_words` with a deliberately dirty final word and asserts padding bits are zero (and that popcount/equality are correct). Cover word-boundary lengths (1, 63, 64, 65 bits).
- [hard] REQ-04: Full `cargo nextest --profile ci` and clippy pass.
title: Enforce tail masking in BitVec::from_words
